question: Should OpenClaw permanently retain this bounded set of restart provenance metadata in the shared state database, and what inspection/deletion contract should operators be allowed to rely on?
rationale: The implementation can enforce redaction and ordering, but code review cannot decide whether client, device, session, task, config-path, and restart-preflight metadata should become a supported durable product record.

options.title: Approve the bounded ledger
options.body: Accept the closed-code, redacted 512-row restart ledger and document its supported fields, inspection path, and retention semantics before merge.

options.title: Narrow the durable contract
options.body: Retain only event type, source, timing, mode, and outcome while dropping correlatable client, device, session, task, and config-path metadata.

options.title: Keep diagnostics transient
options.body: Decline the dedicated table and use existing logs, traces, and diagnostics exporters for restart attribution.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded ledger
recommendation.body: Accept the closed-code, redacted 512-row restart ledger and document its supported fields, inspection path, and retention semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The related audit proposal provides the strongest available evidence of ownership over the durable metadata and retention direction.
